title: Maharashtra judicial employees protest for pay scale parity
seoTitle: Mumbai judicial staff protest pay parity

tea.why: Subordinate court employees are protesting to demand pay scale parity with employees working in the High Court.
tea.want: The protesters want the state government to approve a pay scale revision proposal that has been pending since January 2025.
tea.changed: Oct 16: The Maharashtra State Judicial Employees Federation launched a two-day protest involving black-ribbon demonstrations.

summary: The Maharashtra State Judicial Employees Federation has initiated a two-day protest across the state to demand pay scale parity for subordinate court employees with their counterparts in the High Court. Starting October 16, 2026, serving employees have been performing their regular duties while wearing black ribbons. Additionally, retired judicial employees are participating in sit-in protests outside District Collector offices. According to the Bombay City Civil & Sessions Court Judicial Employees Association, the proposal for pay revision has been pending with the Chief Minister’s Office since January 2025. The federation has urged the state government to expedite the approval process. This action marks the second phase of an agitation that began on September 16, 2026, as employees continue to seek a resolution to their long-standing demands.
organizers: Bombay City Civil & Sessions Court Judicial Employees Association
demands: Approve pay scale parity with High Court employees
Expedite the pending pay revision proposal
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Maharashtra State Judicial Employees Federation began the first phase of their agitation.
The second phase of the protest began with employees wearing black ribbons and retired staff holding sit-ins.
